question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: Pretty neutral. Honestly, 2022 didn't end on a very great note for me. I was dealing with a personal loss which was a pretty major blow to my emotional sanity. 2023, well, was a year of growth. A year of trying to shed old layers, falling back to square one, breaking old patterns, trying new things, feeling light again and what not. I started off with winning an inter-college writing competition, where I had to write a story on the theme ‘comedy of errors'. Comedy truly ain't my thing, but I decided to give it a shot, and voila, I actually bagged the first position! I visited a very unbelievably lovely and scenic place in March and it totally ended up becoming my favourite travel destination so far. (Guess the place, maybe?) I also tried cheesecake and ramen (seperately, ofc) for the very first time. Ramen became an instant favorite and I can't stop going back to it. I befriended a very sweet person and I do feel exceedingly blessed to have her as a part of my life. She's only 7 but we vibe like crazy. I graduated. I learnt how to drive. I cooked a lot of exotic and regional Indian dishes. Cooking is kinda becoming my favorite way to pour out my creativity. I made a lot of personalised scrapbooks and cards for my friends on various occasions. I realised that art has always been my thing and reconnecting with it really made me feel at peace. I binged an AMAZINGGGG popular sitcom, and oh boy, I'm in love with it. I can't stop talking about it to everyone but I would let y'all guess which series I'm talking about. (There's a hint in this answer) Looking back I feel that 2023 had indeed been wonderful to me. There were also various setbacks that I'm not proud of, lots of hanging on to the past, staying stuck in the same pathetic loop and lots of wasting my time. I'm still often vulnerable but now I'm more or less okay with it. I guess I know I'll deal with it ’cause I've done it before. I developed several methods to deal with my crippling mental health (tried Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and I'd highly recommend it to anyone who's in need of some help) I still have the same 2–3 people to cling to when the going gets tough. It's funny and wholesome at the same time because I know nobody else would have dealt with all that I've been, the way they did, and happily continue to do <3 I basically didn't write or read anything this year, but I'm trying to get back at it. Not the writing part, but the reading, yes. Overall, I don't know if this was a good enough analysis of my year or if I did make any sort of progress, but I lived every day. Like literally, lived. Felt every emotion that came my way, irrespective of whether it made me feel like I'm floating or crushed me to irreducible bits. And I guess, at the end of the day, that's what being alive is. And oh, the lesson I got out of 2023? Life is chaos, success is totally arbitrary and confidence is everything :)) Juveria

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: The start was bad, but the end was superb. ▪️Just like every other year, this year too, I didn't qualify for UPSC. My goal of becoming an IFS is still incomplete. But I will not give up on it 🙂. ▪️My novel is still incomplete. I aimed to get it published by the end of this year. But that’s okay. Maybe next year 😅. ▪️No luck in finding any groom for marriage. Maybe it’s far away from what I am aiming for (IFS), but I am still very happy that I got this opportunity. First, my years of hard work finally paid off and at least now I am doing something and earning. It’s better than sitting at home. Second, this job brought lots of changes in my personality. 🌞Being highly introverted, I was very shy to talk and face the public; my confidence level was negligible and I was (or still I am) a highly sensitive crybaby. But after joining this job, I could notice the changes in me. Even though I am blessed with a loud voice, my voice couldn’t even reach the customers from my counter. And it was all because of my low confidence that made my voice shaky. I literally had to stand every time to communicate with them. But with time, I have gained a considerable amount of confidence in myself and now I communicate easily. Soon my voice will echo in the whole post office (just kidding). Now, I deal with the public without any fear or shyness. 🌞Another change that I noticed in me. I had trouble adjusting to the new place and it took me days and months to adjust. But just yesterday itself, I was told to go to another post office as there was a shortage of employees there. At first, I was like “why me?” All along the way, I kept thinking about how I was going to deal there, how I would adjust with new people, what if I messed up something, etc. I was very stressed and nervous but when I reached there and the moment I was assigned my work, I adjusted automatically and started working right away even though the place and people were completely new to me. They were quite happy with my work and said I was welcome anytime there :) 🌞One more change this job brought in me - I finally started attending the phone calls and talking. I personally hated phone calls, especially the unknown numbers. I always neglected them. But I knew I would have to pick them up when my colleagues or boss would contact me and also someone else from other offices whose numbers are not saved in my phone. And yes, now I do attend phone calls - known, unknown, all types :) 🌞 being new, I made mistakes while working. My old self would have cried badly over this. But here, I learned to keep my crybaby personality aside and just find ways to correct my mistakes. 🌞 this job is making me learn something new every single day and I am grateful for that. Maybe, this job will prepare me to become a good IFS (personality-wise 🙂). Happy New Year :)

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: Well, it was a year of mixed experiences for me. The year started with my class 12th pre-board examinations at school, where I scored a decent 83 %, followed by JEE Mains first attempt, where I scored an unprecedented 93.44 percentile. I know, that 93 percentile is not a very good score, but I was satisfied, since to be honest, I had not studied a single line for JEE for the past 4 months. I was so ill-prepared for boards, that I decided to sacrifice JEE for the meanwhile and devote myself completely to pre-boards and boards preparation. I am so glad that my parents, after some initial disagreements, happily supported my decision. My board examinations started in February and continued till March, upon the completion of which, I had to immediately jump aboard the ship of JEE Mains preparation once again. I studied as much as I could in just one month’s time, though I would admit that I could not give my 100 % in the preparations due to some mental health issues. I did selective study, and laid more emphasis on revision. However, the lack of enough practice and attempting enough mock tests ultimately cost me on the final day, where I lost at least 25 marks due to carelessness and ended up scoring just 94.04 percentile. The results came out on April 29th, and my WBJEE exam was scheduled for 30th April. So, I had little time to regret. I quickly transported myself mentally to the domain of WBJEE. I honestly had not studied anything extra for WBJEE, except going through PYQ’s, attempting 3 mock papers, and learning a bit of Maths from my uncle, who is a high school Maths teacher. I knew that I had nothing to lose but much to gain, if I flunked all the rest of my examinations, at least I would be getting into NIT’s. As I was relieved of all the pressure of securing a good college, I just wrote the WBJEE exam to the best of my abilities. Little did I know, at that time, that a single paper would change the course of my life. Well, let it be a surprise for the time being! After WBJEE got over, I took a 3 days’ break during which I attended my cousin’s wedding, which greatly refreshed me from the mental fatigue owing to the happenings of the past few days. Being a general category student, 94 percentile score meant that I was eligible to appear for JEE Advanced. I was at crossroads, coming to this stage. I analyzed all my options, and decided that if I focused on CUET and IAT (IISER Aptitude Test) examinations, the return of investment would be far greater than if I prepared day and night for JEE Advanced, and I was right! I should admit that the month of May was one of the best months of the year. The surprises started with my board results being declared on 14th May, where I scored 96 %, much more than my expected 90 %. My CUET went incredibly well, which earned me priceless seats at both Delhi University and Banaras Hindu University, though I did not choose them for reasons you would come to know of soon. The biggest surprise would arrive on the 26th of May, 2023 (I shall remember this date all my life). My WBJEE General Merit Rank came out to be 1619, my expectations got clean bowled this time! I was expecting a meagre 4000 rank. My parents, family members and myself were simply elated! How a single incident can transform the life of a person! It was not very hard to firmly decide at this moment that I would attend one of India’s premier institutions, Jadavpur University, for engineering. Having got much more than I could have hoped for, I casually sat for JEE Advanced and for IAT. JEE Advanced, as expected, resulted in failure, though it did not hurt me even a bit. IAT would throw even more surprise, since my AIR came out to be 2386 (which bagged me a seat in IISER Bhopal), despite my casual attitude before and during the examination! After a grueling counselling process, I finally became a student of Mechanical Engineering at the prestigious Jadavpur University. My parents were so happy and satisfied with my performance that they took me to new places like Nabadwip, Mayapur, Kamarpukur, Tarakeshwar, Sunderbans, Digha, Belur Math, Botanical Gardens, Dakshineshwar, etc. It felt so emancipating to be travelling after three years totally stationed at home. This year also witnessed the first episode of our family Durga Puja at our village! Some tragic incidents took place too, like the death of our local boy, Souraneel, in a horrible road accident and the infamous ragging incident leading to death of a fresher student at Jadavpur University. My university life has started on an excellent note. In the first two months, I have had the fortune of meeting some of the most talented students and some of the most brilliant professors of the country. In the end, I shall not be exaggerating if I say, that the year 2023 will remain etched in my memory forever. Wishing all my readers good health and good luck for the upcoming year! Hari Om Tat Sat! Om Shanti!

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: ‘Spirtuality, Sensuality and everything in between’ 2023 has been one of the lightest years in a long time. No big highs. No big lows. It went quite smoothly. 2022 was like a Paheli. It started on a high, like going home after long covid break, meeting ex for the first time after a really long long distance relationship, and travelling to some new places with her and ended on a low with figuring out the sudden acid refluxes, endoscopy and getting diagnosed with GERD. Compared to this, 2023 had no extremes. It was relatively a fun ride. Here are some events: The GERD subsided with no medication. With minor changes— no heavy dinners, no soft drinks and a better sleep schedule—and no medication, it was sorted completely. Maybe, it is a warning bell. A beautiful 2-year relationship with Ex ended in 2022. I strongly believe in two things, when it comes to relationships. One, People leave, memories stay. Two, never force longevity on relationships. Hence, after it came to a nice closure, I was more excited about the new phase and the next person. One nice part about 2023 was meeting new girls in different apps, talking to them and endless conversations. Ever since college, I always loved knowing about women through conversations. It was like reading a novel or a personal diary. As all the time and energy in the past two years was utilised to focus on one person, 2023 suddenly gave that space to more women. 14-Day Yoga Vacation at Madurai. It was long-term plan and finally, 2023 made it happen. Joined a yoga ashram in Madurai and stayed there for 14-days. Bhajans twice a day, satvik food, yoga and meditation sessions, cold showers, silent moments, paying antyakshari in the nights during power cut. It was easily the best experience that year. It felt like a heaven. I discovered a lot of my strengths, physically, mentally and spiritually. Also, during that stay, there were 13 other people from different countries— some teachers, some students— from different age groups, from different walks of life. The ashram was near empty before and after my stay. So, kharmically, it so happened all of us were there at that point of time. I made some wonderful connection. Some of them are still in touch. 30-Day trip to Europe. I went to Germany in 2022. Going there back in 2023 was like reunion. I couldn’t do it last time due to time constraints. So this trip began with fulfilling those regrets. It also felt like starting where I left. Have been a very big fan of tantric massages. This time, I also got to travel to Iceland, Venice, Milan and Belgium. It was other end of the spectrum compared to the yoga trip—loud, sensual and adventurous. Meeting friends. Most of my close friends are from school. We used to meet every year after school. Due to covid and other travel schedules, we couldn’t have a proper get-together. This time we all could make it. Not one, but twice. It was amazing. Also, got to meet one of my closest friends since school in Belgium. It proved to be the best part of the trip. Also, finally got to meet in person one of my favourite longtime quora friends. Have been talking with her since 2020: She used to tell about her tamil then-boyfriend-now-husband while I used to tell her about my malayali then-girlfriend-now-ex. Hearing about my grandfather’s death as I landed in Iceland. Though it was sudden and unexpected, I didn’t have any regrets or major missing. I have a very practical view about life and quite sure that everyone of us will leave one day or the other. Hence, I prefer painless and quality death over long, painful life. So, I kind of felt relieved that he passed away peacefully in sleep at home, while he was still active, agile and working. The final thought was the same I had with my ex- People Leave. Memories Stay. As I had lot of memories and there was completeness in his life, it didn’t bother me much. So thus 2023 has been a nice, smooth ride. It was like a light popcorn movie. Excited to see what 2024 has in store.

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: I wish to note down month-wise major happenings of the year. May be some years down the lane, when I read this answer, it will make me smile. January- I went for my first trip with a group of strangers to Gokarna. It was a very different experience for me. I spent a night looking at the stars at a beach, nothing short of magic. I connected with myself. It was so relaxing. I stayed away from any screen and unnecessary noise in my head. February- I got married. It was a bittersweet feeling. Though I was living away from my family, officially moving away from them made me really emotional. I moved into another family and have a new set of parents now. I have many more responsibilities. March- I traveled to one of my dream destinations- Kashmir. It was actually like a dream, so serene and so beautiful. It is truly heaven on Earth. Met really sweet people. Also spent a few days in my in-law’s house and enjoyed the new bahu phase. April- I was invited by a coaching institute to give a talk on my career and guide the students. It was another thing that I always wanted to do. I had taught and guided thousands of students virtually but doing that in person was something I will always cherish. May- I went for my first work trip as Assistant Director to Diu. It was such a nice experience. I got more respect, something I yearned for being a group B officer. When you at a lower post, you just look up and want to do better. I was finally feeling the way I always wished. Obviously, I wish to go higher but I am so grateful for what I had and what I have now. June- I got my first car. Now this was not even in my wildest dreams but somehow, we felt the need for a lifestyle upgrade. I had added another life-skill, I learnt how to drive. It is so liberating to be free to move anywhere I wish. July- It was another work trip to Mahabalipuram. Meanwhile, we were moving away from the newly-married phase to setting up a house and owning up responsibilities. Every few days felt like new. There was constant change. August- We went to Delhi for my birthday and I threw a barbie-themed party for near ones, only to regret later looking at the bill amount. I remember writing a quora answer about the same. September- My sister and brother-in-law came to Bengaluru and I had my first road trip in my car with them. Driving for about 200 km at a stretch on the highway with blasting music and everyone singing along was such an experience. I can never forget that. Every moment from that trip is so precious. October- It was the month when my best friend gave birth to her daughter, Jisha. I remember how I cried happy tears the day she gave me the news of her pregnancy. When I finally held her in my arms, I got all answers to the questions I had. I always wondered why people make such a big deal out of having kids and being a mother. I can not wait to watch her grow up. November- My first Karva Chauth, diwali after marriage- good time with family. I also got the chance to work at Delhi office for some 15 days and attend a global conference in Ahmedabad. I also got to know more about the scope of fisheries in the country. It is a lesser known but an immensely important sector. December- Lastly, I went to attend a destination wedding in Kerala. Had another road trip with friends for the New Year’s and mostly, had a lot of fun. Among all these good parts that I would like to take away from this year, I also need to acknowledge certain negative emotions I felt. I was not alone anytime of the year but I did feel lonely and lost at times. I still have a few regrets and wanted to work towards some betterment. I kept procrastinating the entire year, almost. This is just adding to regret. This year, 2024, I will try not to accumulate any regrets. I will learn another life-skill: the art of saying no. I will stand up for myself and things that I wish to achieve. I have enough time and I don’t have enough time- It all depends on how I choose to spend my time. question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: Full of extreme downs, sufferings and beyond painful life lessons. I attempted CA Inter Group 2 exam for the 4th time in May 23′. Since COVID I’ve been studying at home with pre recorded lectures, zero social life and non existent friends. My home is another broken story of its own, faced a lot of trauma and emotional abuse, but I guess I’m used to it since childhood so nvm. Since the beginning I had a hate relationship with CA, my heart was so not into it, but I was just being forced to keep going and so I did. If you start something on a bad note, it isn't hard to guess what the results are gonna be! And just like that, I failed in my 4th attempt also. My parents were so disappointed in me, all my relatives said a 100 bad things behind my back and some to my face. I was repeatedly told I won't succeed in life. At this point my self esteem was so low and my confidence in life was so shattered that I hardly took care of myself. On some days I even felt like I don't deserve the food I’m getting to eat because I'm such a failure. I just wanted to drop out of CA since always, but because of family pressure I just couldn't. I never had any plan B. I used to listen to all the taunts and insults that were thrown at me, because I thought that's what I deserved. My mental health went to negative 3000. I used to vomit every morning, had constant headaches and my specs power doubled. I lost so much weight. At this point in my life I thought I didn't deserve to live because I wanted to do nothing. I used to feel guilty that I'm just a waste of a person. I didnt even realise on my birthday that it was my bday until my mother wished me. I didn't even acknowledge it. Everyone, including myself was just fed up with me. So much self loathing I was in. Then after May attempt’s results I was again asked to reattempt the November exam. I was so numb at that point of time that I just agreed to whatever was told me to do. I spent next 4 months preparing for the exam in horror. I was so afraid of results by this time that I even feared attempting the exams. I spent the 4 months in constant stress, my hair started turning white. I was diagnosed with thyroid. I used to throw up constantly. I had beyond painful periods, due to all the stress I took. I started believing that CA is like the end of the world. If I’m not able to clear it, I will never succeed in life or even be able to earn any kind of money. During this time tensions were very high in my home. My parents used to constantly fight and the atmosphere was just so negative. But I somehow survived. Then came the exams, and it even got worse this time. I was so nervous that I couldn't remember anything. It felt like the exam room was closing up on me, I felt suffocated. I got this ‘me against the world’ feeling over there. Such a waste of effort. Life itni mushkil hoti bhi nhi hai jitni meine banali thi khud k liye. I just somehow gave the exam. After that, I myself decided now I’m going to listen to myself and do what my heart wants. I didn't enroll in an Articleship despite a lot of pressure. I applied for a lot of jobs, on the basis of my Bcom degree and skills. And after 1.5 months of struggle I got a job as a Financial Analyst in a US Based startup. I also work at an NGO part time as a digital marketer and project manager. And I’ve decided to focus on my work for January 2024, since I want to take a break from studies for a while. Post that from Feb I’ll start preparing for CAT, since I have a decent profile of 9/9/8 general category, female, now getting experience in finance. I feel very grateful for how life has turned out in the last two months. I'm grateful for the thankful perspective I have post the extreme stress phase. I'm hoping that I’ll have more strength to deal with life’s situations from now on. I'm hoping that in 2024 I become stronger and more capable. I donated half of my first salary towards meals for underprivileged people through a project the ngo I work for runs. It has given me some sense of purpose in life. I know I have wasted a lot of time in my prime career years, but I’ve decided to let the bygones be the bygones. I'm not gonna cry over spilt milk. I'm currently working two jobs and touchwood liking both of them. I'm not sure whether or not my decision is right, but I'm not going to over think about it and keep working hard.
author: Anjali

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: A Rollercoaster Ride Let me start from Dec 2022. In a very brief format. Dec 2022: I went to Vaishnodevi with my family because I got my 1st job at Siliguri, West Bengal. It was a mannat. Jan 2023: It was expected that the SSC CGL 2022 Mains was going to happen in March and I don't wanna stuck at Siliguri at lower grade pay so I decided to apply for extension for 3 months from Jan to March. Feb 2023: Whole month went in preparation of mains and the excitement of leaving home for the very first time and live alone in a completely strange city. When I wasn't studying then I was searching on youtube about Siliguri and how it's near to Darjeeling, Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim…all the tourist places. March 2023: Exam went well and I booked the tickets of Rajdhani. Rajdhani takes approx 22 hours from Delhi to New Jalpaiguri (NJP). Did a little bit shopping. Reached Siliguri on 26th March and reported on duty on 27th March. April 2023: I had gone with my bhai. Searched rented apartments, food, which road took where, remember all the places, spots, some identity to remember from where to take left or right. Bhai stayed for one week only. May 2023: I literally cried for 2 3 months straight everyday cause of loneliness. There were all male staff (all are 50+) and I was the only young lady there, plus I lived alone in a rented flat. No friends nothing. I joined gym so that I could make some friends. But still I wasn't happy. Missed home plus the task of cooking your own meals for a beginner. I literally lived on cornflakes and milk. In May, SSC CGL 2022 result announced and I got Ministry of Mines. June 2023: Now I know I am not here for a long long time so I started enjoying my own company. Hopping cafes alone, having my meal alone, exploring places, I went to Kurseong, Shivkhola etc alone through public transport. Slowly liking office environment too, all were so nice and treated me like a child. Almost every other day, office colleagues brought me something to eat, asked me what I had for breakfast, lunch, suggested me good places to visit or lunch. July 2023: In all these months, I came to and fro to Delhi to many times, sometimes to give exams, for document verification of Phase IX examination etc etc. I travelled through Rajdhani, other trains too, flights etc. I feel really blessed that in all these months, I literally travelled through flights for about 10 12 times (a little exaggeration) and everytime I got window seat somehow. I love love love looking at the clouds and thanked God everytime I had that view. August 2023: A new young male joined office, 2 years younger to me from Kolkata and finally I got some company. We explored malls, cafes, etc. Btw landlord aunty and her mother-in-law (dadi) were two great companions at that rented flat. I received Lett for document verification of ministry of mines at Geological survey of India, Kolkata. In August, I went to Kolkata from Siliguri. Sep 2023: Applied for Technical Resignation. Ganesh Chaturthi….whole city was decorated, lights. My emotions went haywire. I started loving this city, scared of going to a new place and settling again, learning which way go where, make new friends, what if I won't be able to make friends,etc etc etc. Oct 2023: Durga Pooja vibes. It was so magical. Every nook and corner of this city was lighten up. It was so mesmerizing to my eyes. I couldn't even describe it. On 31st Oct I relieved from my first office. It was a mixed feeling. My landlord aunty was crying. This is what i have earned in all these months …lots of love, respect, experiences, living alone, travelling alone, eating alone, vibing alone. I shot so many dance videos at my apartment, entertaining myself, shopping alone. I can proudly say that Siliguri makes me live with myself. I no longer seek company for every small small things. I developed so much self confidence and didn't hesitate to ask questions. Travelled solo in trains for at max 25 hours alone and I felt safe. Thanking Mahadev throughout these months, every single day, every minute. Nov 2023: I joined Geological survey of India under Ministry of Mines at Hyderabad. Again bhai accompanied me. This time it all went smoothly as if Mahadev wanted to teach me some things and that i learnt at Siliguri and now I am blessed with everything I want. I got apartment very easily, in just one day, got some really good company. And and and phase IX result announced and I got selected. So again need to leave this place. Hyderabad was a very short and sweet period in this year. It gave me everything i craved when i went to Siliguri. I made some really great friends there. Explored a little, didn't get much time and got relieved in just 1 and half month from Hyderabad. Dec 2023: I joined at Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Shastri Bhawan at New Delhi. Finally ghar❤️ Though I didn't get my posting till yet. I just joined at Ministry. Hope I will get home only. Now I am not scared of leaving home. 2023 makes me understand that leaving comfort zone is important, that studying, jobs etc is a very small part of our life, though really important, but what makes our journey easy and happy is a bunch of people. I literally thanked Mahadev for each and every thing i went through this year. Though i cried a lot but laughed more than that. I had more pictures in my phone of Hyderabad than that of Siliguri. I had more memories of Hyderabad than Siliguri because of the people (company) I got. I stopped praying like I want this etc etc. Instead I started showing gratitude for everything. 2023 gave me Financial Stability. I left home for the very first time in all these years and I trust the magic of Universe.
author: Meenakshi Mathur

answer_text: Starting like a falling drop of dew, I stood still as the time flew, Or perhaps not, maybe I gild with the time, Blind to the forthcoming failure, I was heavy on the wine, The wine gulped in celebration of the procrastinated victory, Started on an intoxicated note, the darling January… . question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: Some years are good because, therein, you enjoy life to the fullest, accomplish longstanding personal goals, and see the hard work of years past prove worthwhile, with that which you had imagined the future to be, comes to fruition in a seemingly serendipitous turn of events. 2023 was not one of those years. However, in order for the aforementioned years to occur, some need to be sacrificed into becoming the ‘years of hard work’ which lead to an ultimate goal. 2023 might have been one of those years. I hope. I began this last year as a student at a Bible college which I didn’t really want to attend (and, admittedly put very little academic effort into), however, by being there, I grew in my personal faith journey in ways that I previously could not only have not imagined, but would have looked down upon, had I seen in others. I finally understood the concept of ‘faith’ and how it complements, rather than contradicts, an empirical understanding of the universe. Somewhat ironically, around this same time, I had been struggling with rather adversarial anxiety, which, at times, felt crushing and preventative of any productivity or happiness. Nevertheless, I persisted, and made progress on the anxiety front, simply by recognizing that there was a problem, and that the problem wasn’t me, but something that was attacking me. At this time, I didn’t have any concrete plan for the future, as my attempt to enlist is the Army National Guard, so as to fund a more standard college education, the summer prior had failed, and, while I enjoyed the spiritual community found where I was at, I didn’t (and still don’t) envision myself standing on the other side of the pulpit. I briefly attempted to become a firefighter, and, rather characteristically, that failed due to my failure to check my e-mail. Presently, the ability to join the Guard opened back up, so I finished the semester at that school and then left for Basic Training ten days later. There’s not much to say about the ensuing ten weeks other than that it was simultaneously the best and worst experience of my life. Put into a place of constant exertion with the big scary hat looming over my head, I managed to be the as fulfilled I ever have been, knowing that I was at least doing something that was worth doing. I suspect my mind needs real pressure to function or else it will invent some pressure of its own. While at BCT, I also managed to read over 2/3 of the Bible, and, through the base chapel, discovered the Anglican church, which I now attend. During my subsequent schooling, I continued to excel, being awarded Distinguished Honor Grad at the end of my training cycle. It’s cliche to say, I know, but the values that the military instills are incredibly useful when it comes to learning to live as an adult, if you’re willing to learn them, and I feel that I have. Then, for the last couple of months, I have worked for my dad’s landscaping company (as well as attending monthly drill with my unit) in order to save up money before, once again, beginning college in a week. This hasn’t been the most pleasant experience of my life, given that this isn’t at all the sort of work which I enjoy, and that I don’t have any sort of social circle, with all my friends either being at various colleges or military bases around the United States Europe, and the Middle East. However, sometimes you just have to grind, and my bank account is thanking me right now. I like variety, and the past 12 months have given me a lot of it. I enjoy thinking about the fact that some people my age only graduated high school nine months ago and are now in their first year of higher education. While that’s great for some, I’m the sort that needs to fail in order to grow, and only, with constant trial and error can I feel fulfilled. Hopefully 2024 sees my hard work and development paying off, though, if it doesn’t, I feel entirely prepared to attack whatever obstacles may come my way.
author: John Oliver

question_title: (2) How has 2023 been for you? - Quora
answer_text: Full of changes, firsts-and-lasts, and sentiments! 2023: A Watershed Year of My Life This year will stand apart in my memories because of so many special moments interspersed. This is my last year in school. This is my last time regularly meeting with my school friends. This is my last time in my comfort haven. Soon, I will be off to college, an eye on the future ahead, realising the true essence of adulting. Here’s how I changed. >>I learned to laugh more easily Once upon a time, I held my morals rather too stringently. I used to be offended at the slightest grey jokes immediately. Nothing was ‘just joking.’ Stand-up comedy on dark topics was something I avoided keenly. This year, some of my company changed. Talking with these new people with a great sense of humour, I faced an option. To stay offended every moment, Or, to partake in the jokes and enjoy them along (including those aimed at me). The former option left a bad taste in my mouth. So, I gave a shot at loosening up. My days are much more funnier and wholesome now. What’s more, I learned to take jokes at one’s own expense gracefully. Laughing has innumerable benefits, from improving your mood to increasing your lifespan. This year, even in my lowest times, I could laugh, and boy, did it help! >>The power of perseverance We love instant results, instant food, instant energy. Trusting the process doesn’t go well with our instincts. We leave our goals unfinished because we are obsessed with the immediate. This year, witnessing the power of perseverance inspired me throughout. I know someone who has been working hard for the end for years. There have been times to celebrate and there have been times to despair; the person has kept going unceasingly. As a parable, life poses distractions from the goals you wish to accomplish. Hold onto your commitments and your destination will feel closer. Flicker like lights, and so will your dreams. Self-discipline is the only magic which can happen in your life. Tenacity wins over sporadic bursts of inspiration. >>I understood my emotions rather than bash them I have always felt life with an open, bleeding heart. The good times get transformed into stupendous because of my positive perception and gratitude. However, even slight disturbances in my normal life have made me panic. As I matured, I learned to regulate my emotions. Life’s transient. Almost nothing that happens is going to bother me in the long run. I have grown less afraid of imperfection (and hence facing disapproving looks); I wouldn’t even remember them by the next week. Whenever my heart tears, I let myself sulk rather than shut it up. Life will have thorns. I must embrace the fact than always expect sunshine. I don’t feel things any less, but I have stopped overanalysing them. I find it preferable for my emotions to run through my veins before they go away. How did you change this year?

I remember I had written a fictional post here and sent it to Divyansh Mundra and I got a reply from him appreciating it. Safe to say, that was THE highlight of my month. May Coaching starts online. AND after a lot of anticipation, board results were finally declared (secured 97.2% heehee). June After the batch allocation test, coaching starts offline. Well who knew this would have been the end to my seemingly happy, normal year? July 9 July 2023 - this is where the real drama starts. The people closest to me, my support system, my grades - basically everything I had nurtured and invested my heart and soul into - I could see that shattering right in front of me. The toughest phase I had to endure. I still have no idea how I managed to survive through that turmoil. My birthday being exactly a week later made things even worse. August Reality hits in. I realize I can't just hold on to things or individuals who don't want to stay. Some things have to be let go off. I can’t fix others. Grades start dropping - not as significant to others, but I knew. I knew I wasn’t giving in my 100% even if I wanted to. Health issues start popping up and I start falling sick pretty often (which I suspect, increasing stress levels, had a major role in). September Realized that these 2 years are going to be the most crucial years of my life and I cannot waste time this way. The choices I make now would have a huge impact on my future. I didn’t want myself 2 years later looking back at my old self, with any sort of regret. October Finally decided to prioritize myself for once. I had been living in a perpetual fear of losing someone who eventually did leave. And I could do absolutely nothing. And well, the happiestttttt part of the month, the week I look forward to every year, was Durga Puja. That pujo pujo feeling>>> November Found evidence of getting my trust broken by someone really really close to me. Even “devastated” would be an understatement of what I felt. answer_text: VERY HAPPENING! I absolutely loved the chaos and turmoil that I went through this year. A proper routine is too mundane for me and I absolutely love the fear and thrill I got to experience at the start of 2023. (I filled the CAT form during WFH and I gave Kolkata as my interview city but later my workplace called me back to Bangalore 🌚). Coming to the interviews, now when I think about those moments, I seem to enjoy them. But, my heart was always in my mouth when I was in those moments. I remember asking my mom the night before every interview that what would happen if I don't go for the interview. She would reply, “Nothing much. Just you won't be part of a great B school.” My mom accompanied me to every exam and every interview. Most of the IIM interviews happened in 4 or 5 star hotels which were a little far from my house so we used to take cabs. During the cab journey, my mom would teach me about Kolkata, the route we were taking to reach the hotel, the history of the hotel and what not. I would ask her to quiz me about various current affairs I read. She would make sure I have covered most topics we thought were important. Those cab journeys were more eventful than the interviews themselves! Fun Fact: While waiting for my interview to get over, she would click pics of the hotels as a reminder that she got to visit these hotels because of me and of course, post on FB. 😂😂 Next came the waiting for the results. I remember I’d sulk days waiting for results and playing our countless scenarios in my head. I used to spend my time chatting useless stuff with other aspirants on the Catking groups but that gave me some real good friends. They are all in different IIMs and I connect with them so much even without ever meeting them. I think those chats were a source of stress busting for every one of us. While waiting for the results, I had already resigned from my job, so I had nothing better to do. My mom literally pushed out of my apartment to go out with her to various fine dining restaurants. (Yes, she stayed with me in Bangalore, travelled with me to Kolkata, Delhi and Mumbai and back for the entire duration right from my B schools exams). Also, since I do skincare blogging as my hobby, I got to go a brand event for a Spanish skincare brand in Bangalore! Yay!! We got a lot of awesome goodies. Again, I took my mom with me and she obviously, posted about it on FB. 😁 Then came the results. I was lucky to have faced fewer disappointments in terms of my selection to B schools. Then me, my mom and my dad took a trip to Vaishnodevi. Walked the entired 14 km to the top and came down on horse back. My body had never ached this much ever. My feet had literally swollen! Then, I took admission in IIM Calcutta, met new people and the hustle started again during the Summer Internship Process. Again, I was lucky enough to clear the first interview I got so I didn't have to go through a lot of turmoil. Currently, I'm in my 3rd term and it's somewhat chill that what it was in the beginning. I won't claim to be an expert at deciphering the underlying meanings of everyday changes, but there lies a pattern that is answerable to all of life's what-and-why questions. Up until yesterday, I regarded this year as one of the worst of my life, but I quickly came to the conclusion that I cannot categorize it as terrible simply because the outcome did not meet my expectations. I have always hated endings. It just makes me feel sad and burdened to start everything from scratch. But lately I started appreciating the essentiality of endings. And even if everything went well in the beginning and the entire process worked out smooth, there's a possibility of having a messed up ending. Will it make us feel sad? Yes! Can we do anything about it? No! I read a lot this year, thanks to academic necessities, yet learnt the most valuable lesson out of textbook. There are instances when the timing is so bad that no amount of preparation, diligence, or hard effort can pull us out of the misery. And fighting against universe is a sheer waste of energy and efforts. And in moments like this, we are meant to learn acceptance, and not really expect anything in return for our efforts. Somethings are meant to let go, and set back is the pre-cursor of every come back. "To not to expect anything, and accept everything" will be the mantra that I will be sacredly following now onwards. So okay my ending sucked, but the overall months of this year was an absolute splendid one for me. This year was full of so many firsts, that I'll be talking about a lot. It had its fair share of anxious, overwhelming, self-doubt episodes, but in the end I felt content and proud of what I had created for myself so far. Made a few new friends who were wonderful and homies sticked by. Fell in love with the process of becoming something, and understood how balance and habit creates wonders in our life. I realized that in order to create our dream life we don't have to detest our daily obligations. And it can be fun as well, you just got to be patient enough to find the best fit. "The journey is better than the destination, when you get right people behind your back." Also this year marked the last academic year of my UG, so it did made me feel scared on how fast we are ageing in life, and at this pace, we'll soon be strolling around with sticks and dentures. True, a little over the top. I have just begun my 20s...…. There's this pattern in my life, where even if I want to, I practically cannot function well towards the end of the year. And to be not be able to do something productive makes me feel sick. Nevertheless I understood how its a sign of universe to teach me how to pause everything for a while by plugging off the thoughts and thinking activities of the brain. Hence this year I chose to do nothing and to live a little (which I know I'll mess-up on the way, but it's always better to try). ). Like every single season, this one was unlike any other. It healed me, changed me and transformed me into a better person and made me realize that we are way more stronger than what we think we are. Was pretty curious and stressed on what's coming next, but leaving all expectations behind with this year and focusing on the present henceforth. Regards🤍

answer_text: Anxiety is increasing as 2024 approaches. Hello, I am Abhishek Rethe. Right now I am in class 12th, hsc from Maharashtra board. I am very depressed right now. My aunt could not see my grief and she reunited me with my mother. Although they also did not have my mother's address. I came to know that mom is now married, but she does not have children. question_title: (2) Who will win the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023? - Quora
answer_text: I see India as the hot favourites with Australia and England running them closest for this world cup. Points to note :- Players of all these teams play each other in IPL every year, therefore India misses some home advantage. The world cup is being played from 5th October to 19th November which means the overall weather will be pleasant to moderate and not a big problem for foreign players. India travels to 9 venues in league stage while Australia and England travel to 8 cities (with England travelling twice to Ahmedabad in league stage itself), So fatigue factor will remain nearly the same for all three teams. These three teams are the best batting sides of the world currently. Their batting styles maybe different but they have honed their skill over years. With most of them being proven match-winners . According to me, this is the Best playing 11 of the sides, in most of their matches:- Now let’s see who plays whom and the their match locations !! Now let’s dive deeper :- India Strengths:- In-form team, all the batsmen in the top-6 have scored had good game time with decent scores coming into the world cup. Reserve batters Surya kumar Yadav and Ishan Kishan have scored runs which gives India good backup options. Shami with his experience can replace Siraj/Bumrah in any of the 9 league matches . Shami with his skill-set and experience gives India a solid 3rd seam option as well . With inclusion of Ashwin India’s spin bowling looks lethal when combined with Kuldeep and Jadeja. Home Conditions with home crowd support will obviously help India . Weakness :- KL Rahul was very poor with the gloves in the 1st game vs Aus in Mohali. In crunch knockouts this can haunt India. Shardul Thakur has been a touch expensive and even his batting form has been poor recently. Jadeja hasn’t scored big recently or finished/won the game for India in recent times with his batting. Injury concerns always roam around Bumrah and Pandya . And we have noone who can match the caliber of these two individuals . Without them the entire balance of the team gets distorted. Australia Strength :- With Marsh and Warner scoring hefty amounts of runs recently and return of Maxwell Australian batting looks solid with smith and labuschagne in the middle to capitalise and Stoinis and Carey to finish . Australia, In my views has the best trio of experienced fast bowlers for ODI’s currently with Indian trio (Shami, Siraj and Bumrah- if plays together). Australia has the reputation to upgrade their game in knockouts and win key moments . This habit can help in close encounters. Weakness :- Their batting without Head lacks that flamboyance left handedness in the middle. He can play a role of someone like Yuvraj Singh in his team . The sooner he gets fit the better it would be for Australians. They lack spin options . They only have Zampa and Maxwell . In Chennai, Lucknow and Delhi spin can be decisive. The side hasn’t played like an unit . In the run of the world cup , Australians were to busy to test everyone and finding their best 11 . This might make them slow starters in the world cup . England Strength :- Their all-rounders are their biggest strength . With Livingstone, Moeen, Curran and Woakes they have a very flexible batting team . Even Mark wood coming at 11 can hit maximums . Their style of play, i.e treating ODI as an extension of an ODI gives them a very big advantage on batting decks of Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru . Also in Kolkata and Dharamsala. Weakness:- With Adil Rashid as the main spinner and Moeen + Livingstone becoming the 5th bowling option . The bowling looks a little iffy . On tracks of Lucknow and Delhi their batting can easily collapse . They will depend too much on Root and Stokes in these tough situations. With Stokes not bowling . Curran and Woakes will find swinging the bowl difficult , here in India. Wood to play 9 games doesn’t seem possible either . This will put pressure on the batting to always score 30 to 40 extra runs than par .

question_title: (2) Who will win the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023? - Quora
answer_text: I know it may be a bit late to predict the world cup winner or top 4’s as thus far we can clearly see the teams in form and out of form after each team has played 5 matches. My initial prediction for Top 4 at the start of the world cup was 1) India 2) New Zealand 3) Australia 4) England. So, let’s get into the points table, before the analysis is made for each teams So, there were 6 major teams competing for 4 spots: India, New Zealand, South Africa, England, Australia and Pakistan. 4 minnow teams are Bangladesh, Netherland, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan(No disrespect for these 4 nations, they have entertained till now). One interesting point till now is every team has won at least one match out of their 5 games with some notable upsets (Ned vs SA, Eng vs SL, Afg vs Eng, Afg vs Pak). Let’s now individually assess each teams and their chances from the current points table: India They have won 5 out of 5 games till now, which was unexpected as the game vs New Zealand in Dharamshala was one of the games where I thought, India might have struggled to win looking at the absence of Hardik Pandya in such big game and Rohit Sharma and management making a bold move of picking 6 proper batsman, 4 proper bowlers and 1 all rounder in Jadeja. Positives: All 15 players of the team has got some game time and the reserves performed well when given a chance except for SKY who didn’t get a proper game time, thanks to the run out against NZ. Shami is clicking whenever he is called upon. Seeing him is just like an art who has a upright seam and can move ball both ways. Stable top 5 Batsman, although Shreyas finds a way to throw his wicket but all the Top 5 batsman are doing good. Weakness: One of them could be Kuldeep Yadav, don’t get wrong he is doing very well with 8 wickets in 5 matches with an economy of 4.73 which is fantastic. But against New Zealand he was sent for cleaner against Daryl Mitchell(who is a world class batsman). Which takes me to 2nd point that Hardik Pandya’s absence could cost a lot for India in knock outs. Hardik will be back after the match against England which is a good news. Only 5 bowlers strategy could backfire, because a class batting line-up like South Africa could take Kuldeep and Siraj for the cleaner. Here Hardik Pandya provides a cover as a sixth bowler if someone is getting bashed for runs, he is there to give crucial overs. Matches remaining: Against England in Lucknow: Ideally, India should win the toss and look to put scores on the board around 320+ which would make England’s life tough as they have chased down in all the 5 matches. A good chance for SKY to get some runs Predictions: India will win the match (70% chances) Against Sri Lanka in Wankhede: No disrespect to SL but they don’t have a chance to win this one. India should go with Hardik Pandya in place of SKY and Shami in this match keeping the rest line up some. Predictions: India to win the match (80% chances) Against South Africa in Eden Gardens: This is the pitch which has not been used till now and the first match would be Bangladesh vs Pakistan. Eden Garden is a dangerous venue to put South Africa to bat first. South Africa has the best bowling line up along side India in terms of consistency. But it’s their Batting which is making life easier for South African bowlers. Rohit Sharma may need to rescue India if India is batting 2nd. Predictions: India may lose their first match of the campaign. (45% chances of winning) Against Netherlands at Chinnaswamy: They may keep the best line up for the last match post if they get defeated in any of the matches as India would have ambition to keep top spot on the points table. Predictions: India to win the match (80% chances). So, these are the likelihood provided all the players can stay fit for the long tournament. Expecting India with total 16 points out of 9 games. Let’s move to 2. South Africa They have a sparkling light of the tournament. I didn’t expected them to click this good. Seems like a Gujarat Titans debut season in IPL thus far. Unexpectedly got defeated while chasing against Netherland in Dharamshala. They have notched 4 wins out of 5 matches. Positives: They have a very good bowling unit with 2 proper spinners in Maharaj and Shamsi, though Shamsi has been used less till now. I feel Shamsi could be a game changer in spin-friendly conditions. Also they have 6 great quality pacers in their Arsenal which makes them the most sought after bowling unit. Form of Batting unit like De Kock, Van der dussen, Klaasen, Miller, Jansen(All rounder) while batting first they are rampant and putting humungous scores on the board. Weakness: Bavuma has not clicked yet as a batsman, in his place Reeza Hendricks played really well. Let’s see how South Africa management tries to resolve if Bavuma keeps on failing as batsman. South Africa’s chasing woes could come to hit them very hard. Although against Netherland it was very tough chasing in the conditions of Dharamshala. Middle Order has not been put under test by a good bowling line-up. Would be interesting to see how the middle order tackle the bowling unit of Pakistan, New Zealand and India if they are chasing. Matches Remaining: Against Pakistan at Chennai: Spin friendly condition in Chennai, South Africa has gone with Shamsi( actually I am writing this live while watching the match). Pakistan went with Mohd Wasim Jr as an X-factor, let’s see how Pakistan defends the total. It’s a must win match for Pakistan. Interesting stats: 3 out of 4 matches are won here by chasing. Also, it is the same ground where Pakistan lost against Afghanistan. Prediction: South Africa to win this match (60% chance) as Pakistani spinners are not picking wickets in the middle which will favor South African middle order while chasing. Against New Zealand at Pune: Maharashtra is favored for just pace and bounce which kind off helps the team with good horizontal shot playing. This is a tough-one as both teams are kind-off good even without Williamson for New Zealand. Rachin Ravindra has stepped up big time for New Zealand. Prediction: South Africa may lose this one (45% chance of winning) as New Zealand would relish the challenge of chasing down and their top 5 may turn really good for the South Africa. Against India in Eden Gardens: Predicted in the India section for South Africa’s win Against Afghanistan in Ahmedabad: Mostly a highway pitch for scoring tons of runs. South Africa would like to have more matches in Narendra Modi stadium which suits their attack minded batting line up. South Africa would find them comfortable chasing here. Prediction: South Africa to win (80% chance). So, these are the likelihood provided all the players can stay fit for the long tournament. Expecting South Africa with total 14 points out of 9 games. Moving to 3. New Zealand. Consistency, Unity goes synonymous with their performances and expectations are high with this healthy unit. They have lost against India, winning all the other remaining 4 matches. Positives: Top 5 batsman of this team are contributing quite well, just like India. Will Young, Conway, Rachin, Mitchell, Latham all have given their contribution for the team. They have also have a organised bowling unit in Boult, Henry, Lockie and Santner bowling in the mix. As a unit they are most of the boxes. Weakness: Lower middle order has not stepped in quite well, specifically for Chapman. He is a good lad but needs to step up. Even Neesham can replace him giving an additional all rounder option in middle overs. The above pointer leads to the problem of the fifth bowler quota. Basically this is where New Zealand has to be smart to use their fifth bowler maybe in Glenn Philips or Rachin. Matches Remaining: Against Australia in Dharamshala: This would be a cracker at high-altitudes where the fielding would be very difficult for these two units. A close matchup I can see where Australian bowling unit would relish the challenge of stopping NZ scoring huge runs. Prediction: New Zealand may lose this match (40% chance of winning) as Australia would be turn out to be good for them on the day. Against South Africa in Pune: Predicted in South Africa section for New Zealand to win. Against Pakistan in Bangalore: Small ground with Pakistani spinners going for toss, I think New Zealand should take 2 points from this match and venue. Prediction: New Zealand to win this match (65% chance) Against Sri Lanka in Bangalore: Carrying the momentum from previous match in the same venue this should a fetchable win for New Zealand. So, these are the likelihood provided all the players can stay fit for the long tournament. Expecting New Zealand with total 14 points out of 9 games. Moving to 4. Australia: This team has rather looked patchy, they have too many all rounders which has contributed to kind-off less expected outcomes from them. They recovered well after getting an hammering from South Africa and India. So, they have 3 wins out of 5 matches which makes them a good contenders for the Semi-Final berth Positives: Australia has picked the gears at the right time with Zampa being their X-factor after initial bad matches. Zampa is crucial for Australia to click because he is the only frontline spinner of the entire 15 man squad. The ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2023, to be hosted by India, will be the 13th edition of the 50-over World Cup. India will be hosting the quadrennial tournament for the fourth time in its history, and the tournament is set to take place in 2023. Format Ten teams will contest for the coveted trophy. The tournament will follow a similar format to the 2019 edition in England and Wales, with a round-robin stage followed by the knockouts. All 10 teams will compete against each other once in the round-robin stage. A victory earns the winning side two points in every match, while a no-result will mean the sides share a point each. The top four teams at the end of the round-robin stage will qualify for the semi-finals. The winners of the two subsequent semi-finals will contest in the final, where the champion will be crowned. Qualification The ICC Cricket World Cup Super League 2020-23 will be the main qualification pathway for the tournament. History The 2023 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup will be the 13th edition of the tournament. The tournament first took place in 1975 in England. This will be the fourth time that India will be hosting the tournament and the first time that it will be the sole host. They previously co-hosted the tournament in 1987, 1996 and 2011. England are the defending champions heading into the tournament, having won the trophy on home soil in 2019 after defeating New Zealand in a thrilling final at Lord’s. If you still can't have empathy and acceptance for someone who doesn't “look” the way you want them to look, atleast have the decency to not be a troll and keep away. Its embarrassing really. Stopping being co dependent is gonna take the living daylights out of your life. But few smacks and thwacks, and a few mental breakdowns getting admitted to the hospital oughta do it. Its the hard way yes, but if only you had your red flag and strong boundaries radar working, don't worry, you will get there someday. Self worth is the biggest game that you shall have to win. Accept that you can have unhealthy traits too. Continue harbouring insight. Continue working on yourself. Heal from what hurt you, there is no moving forward without that. Great sex doesn't mean a great relationship. My patients come with all sorts of amazing physical intimacy stories with poor emotional intimacy and incompatibility. Even a douchebag can give you an orgasm. Although my patient files are filled with women who never had one. Chemistry doesn't guarantee compatibility. Bare minimum just isn't enough. The vice versa is also true. If you are compatible and yet don't have a good sex life( unless you are asexual and are in a platonic relationship), then you need to sit down and talk about it. Don't go hawwww when it comes to sex. Its the very reason why you are sitting there reading this. Might as well be great at it. Oh buy vibrators. They are these cool sex toys which make you need a man less, or make sex better even if there is a man involved. There should be zero stigma attached to pleasure. Your boyfriend/partner should definitely be gifting you one of those. Also gift it to your female friends. Even if it really messes up with their boyfriend's egos. Do it nevertheless. I do not recommend marriage to anyone. However if you do decide to, I shall definitely be dancing in the sangeet and cheering you on. If you are someone's dirty little secret, and they cant acknowledge you as their partner in public, its simply not worth it, no matter how tempting it sounds. There is absolutely zero time on this earth to be someone's rehabilitation centre. Goes both ways, if your depression spirals out of control, and your partner chooses not to deal with it because its difficult, that's fair too. Its all about how anyone chooses to end things. Its not the end of the world. You will get better. Someone will choose you. Till then, you are there for you. Stronger than ever, Prouder than ever, Calmer than ever. Stop spending money on printed shirts. Let that money go to therapy. The return on investment is immense on the later. Be a part of more queer communities. Trust me they are the most lovable, non judgemental, safe spaces to be in. If anyone is uncomfortable with you being queer or being associated with the queer clubs, you know who to run away from. Anyone who disses women in front of you, and calls himself/herself a self proclaimed feminist, run. Run in real life as well. Marathons, Treks, Hikes. Makes you more confident and less ladylike. Which is the whole point. Solo travelling scares the shit out of you I know. Yet you will do it. It will set you free from the need of wanting anyone. Forgive yourself for the days you were not at your best. When you cried till you looked like a muddy puddle. Or when you begged for love from someone who was just not willing to give it. Or when you were slutshamed for being on a dating app. Feelings are not facts. Being heartbroken is not forever. Standing up for what you believe in, despite the nerve wracking anxiety? Kickass cool. It hurts because you care. And you won't be alive if you didn't care. Also cellulite is ABSOLUTELY OKAY. Remember, Whether you are in a dress or in a suit riding a motor bike, no one can take away your sexiness from you. No one. Breathe in. Its all okay. You have got this. Where is the Miracle God? I cried out aloud. ‘You are the Miracle my child’ God replied.
author: Pallavi Preeti Nanda

question_title: (2) What are some life lessons you learned in 2023? - Quora
answer_text: 2023 has been a tough yet fulfilling year for me. I discovered the realities of life. I learned things I didn't want to learn. Or yet I didn't want to accept. I put an end to my abusive marriage. I carved a path of my own. I rediscovered my love for writing and decided to create a career out of it. I am juggling motherhood, work, and the house together. 2023 taught me never to revolve my life around one person. It taught me to stand up for what's right and stop normalizing the otherwise overlooked issues in society. I learned how important it is to be independent. You don't know what tomorrow holds. If you would tell me a year back, that I would be tackling everything that comes with being a single mother, I would laugh it off. I didn't know how strong I was until 2023. I'm grateful for the year that taught me to be resilient, stick to my values, stand for the right, accept changes, and work harder in life. Sometimes life doesn't go as planned but that's okay. In the end, life is all about acceptance. It's about setting boundaries. It's hard to cut off toxic people but the peace you feel after that, it's worth the effort. So, what are some life lessons I learned in 2023? It's perfectly normal to make choices that do not blend in with the society's expectations. It's important to cut off negative or toxic people from your life. It's okay to prioritize your mental health. Self-love is more valuable than it seems. It is impossible to please everyone around you. You can't help people who don't want to be helped. No relationship is worth that sacrificing your health and happiness.

question_title: (2) What are some life lessons you learned in 2023? - Quora
answer_text: Do things you do not feel ready for yet. Many of the best things in life happen when you say “yes” to things you are scared of, feel not ready for, and that make you uncomfortable. If you, in any way, believe it can be good for you objectively, then do it. Do not let your fear of what may come keep you from experiences that can change your life. Being surrounded by the right people matters so much. That means you must invest into these people and relationships. Give to the people around you and you will get something back. Get out every week. Never stay home for longer than 7 days in a row. You must go out to some event every week, even if it is just a small get together, dinner with your partner, or meeting a friend for coffee. Get out of the house. And no, going to work does not count. You are more amazing than you view yourself to be. We are own worst critics. Try asking other people what they admire in you, and you will likely find things that you find hard to accept. If it’s not a clear “no” then it defaults to a “yes”. When you are contemplating anything that may be good for you, then you only have one chance to give a clear “No”. Whenever there is doubt of whether or not you truly do not want to do it, just do it. This goes along with #1 but is the best way to get out of your comfort zone and push into being a better, braver, and more successful you. Expecting nothing is one of the greatest freedoms you can have. Expect nothing from any date, flirtation, from any interview, interaction, sales call, get together or any interpersonal activity at all. The less you expect the more freedom you feel to act the way you want to. Get out of your head and just do what you can. Love does not have to be romantic. Stop trying to limit the term “love” to only romantic love. You love your friends, family and can love yourself in a non-romantic way. Express more of that and do not worry how it is perceived. Hug your friends, compliment them, tell them how much they mean to you and just share more of what you feel inside. The more you do the better you will feel about yourself. Go at life with everything you have. In every situation, make the most out of it. Do not hide parts of you or limit who you are and live each moment to its fullest. Commit to the experiences you make. You said “yes” to this, so go and live it up!
author: Lukas Schwekendiek

question_title: (2) What are some life lessons you learned in 2023? - Quora
answer_text: 2023 has been one tough year for me. Having said that, I realise that the past year was filled with so much growth, like never before. Failures happen more often than succeses. And they happen to keep you grounded. The moment you get overconfident that you've got it all figured out, that's when it hits you. Pride is stricken down faster, to keep you real. Luck is a very real thing. And it favours a very few. Some people will have it slightly easy than others. If you’re not that lucky like me, don’t worry. You can make your own luck. How? With hard work. Hard work is the foundation for success. There are no shortcuts in life. Along with that, perseverance and discipline are the building blocks for triumph over life. And excuses? Well, they will get you nowhere. No one will pave the way for you to walk on. You have to do that all by yourself. Every gravel, every stone for the path needs to be put down by you, for you. Envy will make you think that the grass is greener on the other side. And may be it is. What to do? Think of ways to make the grass greener on your side. You might take more time than your peers to reach where they are but, it doesn't matter. You grow on your own time. Patience is hard but, its fruitful. Waiting for something to happen can be frustrating but, know this. If you have done your part to the best of your abilities, you will get your desired result. You just have to wait for the right time. Angry outbursts are responsible for most of your blunders. Once you master anger, once you learn to remain calm, there’s nothing that can provoke you to mess things up. Help will come from the most unexpected of places and seldom from the people you expect it from. Be grateful to those people to come to your aid when you need it the most. Not everyone has your best interest at heart. I learned that the hard way. And more often than usual, there are people waiting for you to slip up, to twist your words and to pull you down in any way possible. Work place politics is such a real thing that you will feel that you are back in high school or college, with all the petty gossips, backbiting and shenanigans. Every relationship is temporary. Even friendships. People come and go. So, you have to learn to live without them. You have to learn to enjoy solitude. Letting go isn't easy. Be it people, things or instances. But holding onto them is not going to achieve anything either. If someone wants to leave, let them go. Holding onto them will be more painful. No one has time to listen to your woes. Every single person is preoccupied with their own lives, as they should be. So, at the end of the day, it’s just you alone with your your emotional baggage. You have to suffer alone. You have to go through it alone. And you will rise like a phoenix from the ashes but yes, the burning comes first. You will come out stronger and bolder. Life happens, you grow up. You are forced to be mature, whether you like it or not. Because you can’t think about just yourself anymore. You have a whole family, their expectations and hopes lingering on you. Well, here's hoping that 2024 will be equally enlightening but, slightly less painful. Happy new year, folks!
author: Ditipriya Sarkar

question_title: (2) What are some life lessons you learned in 2023? - Quora
answer_text: 2023 had gone and same with January and half of February of 2024. But the lessons that 2023 had offered is not going anywhere… Let's see what 2023 has offered…. The permanent things are not permanent….they are also temporary…..they only last longer….that's all. No matter how stormy the situation is….how much it has crumbled you…..it too shall pass…… The person who will keep following the crowd….one day shall vanish in the same crowd and no-one gonna remember him….. We need to normalise saying no…. without explanations. People are toxic. Few of them are very good at playing victim card… few of them always ran away from their responsibilities….and most of them are going to with you as long as you are entertaining their interests. Once you said no or incapable of benefiting them they start ignoring you as if you were never existed. We spent most of the time in thinking what people will say…..what people will think…..you know what….for those people you are just like the goal keeper…..no matter how many goals you have saved earlier…..they will only remember the one that you missed. Any person can have only few true friends….rest are only your classmates and colleagues. And we need to normalise this. Stop calling everyone as your friends. Not everyone will celebrate your happiness…. people are envious. Not everyone will be happy for your achievements. So you need to be low profile and don't need to share everything on the social media. You are a demon in someone's story even if you have done nothing wrong and you need to accept that. If they can't beat you….they will try to defame you. We suffer more in our thoughts. The scenarios and “what if” that we play in our mind are more painful than the actual events. All that anxieties for the upcoming things are useless. You can't stop what is going to happen in future. Everything that is in your hand is your reaction and your present. Hardwork pays sooner or later. All we need is to believe in ourselves. There is no heaven or hell….we reap what we sow in this life only… L.W.
